flags.name: output_gate_markdown
flags.seam: internal/promote/promote.go — posts.Validate(postsBase, postSlug), which fails the promote when !res.OK()
flags.description: The Markdown target is content-verified: the staged index.md is re-run through the full disk-facing rule set (metadata fields, date parse, slug/dir agreement, thumbnail shape and existence, body image references, raw-HTML blocklist) and a failure blocks the promote. This is the one output target with a real gate.

flags.name: output_gate_typeset

exceptions.reason: neither target has any content verification. The strongest check is renameToSlug in internal/engine/{tectonic,make4ht}.go, which is an os.Stat existence test and therefore passes for an empty or garbage document. There are no golden files, no testdata fixtures, no text extraction and no integration-tagged tests, so the typeset path is built in CI but never exercised against a sample article. Tracked debt: promote to error once a pdftotext-based smoke gate lands.

flags.description: Declared exception rather than an absent entry: two of this compiler's three output targets ship unverified, and that is now visible instead of implicit.

flags.name: font_integrity

exceptions.scope: all targets — font selection belongs to the author's LaTeX preamble
exceptions.reason: this compiler ships no templates and has no font field in meta.yaml, so typography is chosen entirely by the author's main.tex preamble or a shared snippets-repo preamble. The compiler cannot know the declared family, so it cannot verify identity. Embedding is likewise unverified: tectonic's argv in internal/engine/tectonic.go carries no embedding flag and nothing inspects the result, so the engine default is relied on.

flags.description: Not enforceable here as designed, which is a deliberate consequence of the raw-.tex input model rather than an oversight. Revisit if a font key is ever added to the meta.yaml contract.

flags.name: image_alt_meaningful

exceptions.reason: the Markdown validator checks that every body image REFERENCE resolves on disk, which is reference existence rather than alt quality. imgBodyRE in internal/posts/posts.go matches an empty alt group, so an image written as ![](./images/x.png) validates cleanly today. Enforcing non-empty alt would be a real change in author-facing strictness and belongs in its own PR, not a declaration-only one.

flags.description: Applicable to this compiler's Markdown output and currently unenforced. Declared so the gap is reviewable: the rule is meaningful here, it simply is not gated yet.
